event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Rosie O’Grady’s Dueling Piano Show
event.description:
Every Wednesday, Thursday, Friday & Saturday

You Might Just Be the Star of the Show!

Doors Open at 7:00 PM | Show Starts at 8:00 PM (6:00 PM Every Friday!)

If you’re looking for high-energy entertainment, unforgettable music, and nonstop laughs, Rosie O’Grady’s Dueling Piano Show at Seville Quarter is the place to be in Downtown Pensacola.

Step into the legendary Rosie O’Grady’s Good Time Emporium at 7:00 PM to grab your seat, order a drink, and soak in the lively atmosphere before the show kicks off at 8:00 PM. From the first note to the final encore, this crowd-fueled show delivers Pensacola’s most exciting live entertainment experience.

Featuring four of the South’s top piano players, vocalists, and entertainers, the Dueling Piano Show is a blend of musical talent, comedic timing, and audience interaction. Expect hilarious bits, spontaneous sing-alongs, and your favorite songs by request—plus a few surprises. And who knows? You might just end up in the spotlight!

• The Finest Bar & Wait Staff on the Gulf Coast
• Signature cocktails, cold beer, and a full-service bar
• A fun, interactive vibe perfect for date nights, birthday parties, and group celebrations

Come early, stay late, and be part of a Seville Quarter tradition that’s been making memories for decades.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

 

Boots, Buckles & Boogie

event.title: Sunday Funday
event.description:
Every Sunday Starting at 11:00 AM

Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion, catching up with friends, or simply soaking in a lazy Gulf Coast afternoon, Seville Quarter’s Sunday Funday is Pensacola’s #1 way to wind down the weekend, or kick it into high gear.

We’ve taken everything you love about Sunday and made it unforgettable:

Start Your Day with Seville Sunday Brunch
11:00 AM – 2:00 PM | Palace Café & Courtyard
Our delicious brunch features classic Southern favorites, chef specials, and one of the best Soup & Salad Bars in town, plus our fully stocked Build-Your-Own Bloody Mary Bar, Mimosas, and BOGO bottles of Champagne.

Vibe Irie Reggae – Live in the Courtyard
4:00 PM – 9:00 PM | End O’the Alley Courtyard
Feel the island rhythm every Sunday evening with Vibe Irie Reggae Band, live under the oaks. It’s the perfect setting for great music, cold drinks, and good vibes.

Specials & Courtyard Cookout
Kick back with cold beers, Red Stripe for $3, tropical cocktails, and tasty food fresh off the grill. Great eats, lawn games, and chill vibes all afternoon long. $20 BOGO bottles of Champagne.

Fast Eddie’s Billiards – All Day Sunday
Rack ’em up in Fast Eddie’s Billiards Room with great drink specials and a laid-back, air-conditioned atmosphere perfect for friends and pool sharks alike.

event.title: B.A.R.E. Night
event.description:
Bar and Restaurant Employee Night

Sunday nights at Seville Quarter belong to the hardworking heroes of the hospitality industry! Join us every Sunday, ALL DAY, to celebrate B.A.R.E. Sundays, Pensacola’s original and longest-running Hospitality Industry Night.

This is your day to unwind, relax, and raise a glass with your fellow bar and restaurant professionals. Enjoy special B.A.R.E. price drinks all day long exclusively for B.A.R.E. Card members at the End o’ the Alley Bar — your backstage pass to the best Sunday night in town.

Whether you’re coming off a double shift or just wrapping up a long weekend of service, Seville Quarter is here to celebrate you. Great drinks, great company, and the best Sunday vibe in the city, you’ve earned it.

Not a member yet? Stop by and sign up for your B.A.R.E. Card and start enjoying the benefits immediately.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Bar Bingo
event.description:
8:00 PM in Apple Annie’s | Free to Play!

Every Monday – Bar Bingo at Seville Quarter

Dinner at 5:00 PM | Bingo at 8:00 PM in Apple Annie’s | Free to Play!

Start your week off right with Dinner & Bingo at Seville Quarter!

Come early and grab a bite, Dinner starts at 5:00 PM in Apple Annie’s Courtyard, featuring a full menu of crowd-pleasers: juicy burgers, hot pizzas, wings, fresh Gulf seafood, and more. It’s the perfect way to fuel up before the fun begins!

Then stick around for the wildest Bingo night on the Gulf Coast, Bar Bingo kicks off at 8:00 PM with Seville’s legendary “Good Time Gang” leading the way. It’s free to play, full of laughs, and packed with:

Drink Specials:
• $2.50 Miller Lite Bottles
• $3.50 Bomb Shots
Prizes, Giveaways, & Bar Tabs for Winners!

This ain’t your Grandma’s Bingo (though she’s more than welcome)! Expect hilarious twists, a rowdy crowd, and the kind of good times only Seville Quarter can deliver.
Come for dinner. Stay for the fun. Win big at Bar Bingo!

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

 

Boots, Buckles & Boogie
Tuesday Country Nights at Boss Phogg’s

Every Tuesday beginning October 6, 2026
Dance lessons with Dawn Alexander: 7–9 p.m.
Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie: 9 p.m.–midnight or later

Learn It Tuesday. Dance It All Weekend.

Run. Refuel. Repeat.

Lace up your running shoes and join the Seville Quarter Milers, Pensacola’s most fun and social midweek run! Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just starting out, all levels are welcome to hit the streets of Downtown Pensacola together.

event.title: Noche Tropical – Latin Night
event.description:
Presented by Latin Flavor Entertainment

Every Wednesday | 7:00 PM | Phineas Phogg’s

Wednesdays just got a whole lot hotter in Downtown Pensacola!

Seville Quarter and Latin Flavor Entertainment invite you to spice up your midweek routine with “Noche Tropical” Latin Night, held every Wednesday night in the iconic Phineas Phogg’s.

From 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM, get ready to move your feet with a vibrant Social Latin Dance experience featuring Salsa, Bachata, and Merengue, no partner required! Whether you’re a seasoned dancer or just getting started, this is the perfect night to feel the rhythm and connect with a fun, energetic crowd.

🎶 The night doesn’t stop there!
Once the social dancing wraps, it’s time for “FLAVOR TIME”, as DJ DavidC hits the decks and keeps the dance floor alive with a tropical mix of:
• Latin Pop
• Reggaeton
• Top 40 Latin Remixes
• Tropical Beats from across the globe

🍹 Drink Specials:
Enjoy refreshing Bacardi Rum Flavors Specials and tropical cocktails all night long to help you truly capture the spirit of the islands.

Whether you’re dancing the night away, sipping something smooth, or just soaking in the high-energy vibes, Noche Tropical is the #1 Latin Dance Party in Pensacola, a midweek fiesta you don’t want to miss!

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. event.description:

Super Premium Cocktails

1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine

1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.

4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.description:

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

event.description:

Join us for THE WAITING ROOM: Endometriosis, Body Autonomy, and Collective Care, a free public gathering at Weeksville Heritage Center in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, on Saturday, October 3, 2026.

RESERVE YOUR SPOT

Centering endometriosis education, body autonomy, and our collective responsibility to care for one another, The Waiting Room gathers us to honor the knowledge carried in our bodies and consider what we can build, demand, and practice while we wait for science, health insurance, and government policy to catch up with our lived realities.

The day includes an accessible introduction to understanding endometriosis, a panel discussion, a participatory workshop, community resources, and opportunities to share your story.

Panelists: Dr. Jessica Opoku-Anane, Dr. Monica R. McLemore, Jamila Williams Kane NP, and Shakira K. O’Garro LMHC

Everyone is invited to listen, learn, contribute, and help imagine more expansive possibilities for individual and communal care.

Created and curated by multidisciplinary artist and educator Amyra León, The Waiting Room marks the inaugural public gathering of the Chronic Arts Coalition, a new initiative founded by León to center those living and creating with chronic conditions while reckoning with the chronic conditions of society.

Presented in collaboration with Weeksville Heritage Center, with support from Brooklyn Arts Council and the Endometriosis Foundation of America.

This event is free and open to all ages. RSVP below to reserve your spot.

event.title: Jeffrey Zeigler’s – “We Were Fridays” at Weeksville
event.description:
@

On October 17, 2026, Weeksville Heritage Center and VisionIntoArt invite you to a day-long community experience in Brooklyn. The program weaves together performance, creative workshops, and community conversations that explore the key themes and inquiries of We Were Fridays—cultural memory, Gullah Geechee heritage, diaspora, and intergenerational storytelling.

RESERVE YOUR SPOT

We Were Fridays is an interdisciplinary music project led by cellist Jeffrey Zeigler – a deeply personal exploration of cultural memory and diaspora. It will follow a story that began in the Griot tradition of West Africa, travel to South Carolina by way of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade, then north by way of the Great Migration, and beyond. We Were Fridays explores the music of the Gullah people of the Low Country of South Carolina, a community which to this day has preserved more of their West African linguistic and cultural heritage than any other African American community in the United States. Gullah music has influenced spirituals, gospel, ragtime, rhythm and blues, soul, hip hop and jazz. We Were Fridays will extend this reach into the world of instrumental cello music. Told through cello, electronics, and dance, We Were Fridays will explore forbidden love, fractured lines, and complex legacies.

As covered in The New York Times, We Were Fridays is one of the most significant works of cultural memory and diaspora to come to Brooklyn this fall.

“My father was raised in Philadelphia with no knowledge of his biological family until 1992, when a woman named Burnice Perry contacted him. She became the grandmother I never knew, tracing our lineage back to George Washington Friday. Before she passed, I recorded hours of our conversations; those recordings are the heartbeat of this work…”

– Jeffrey Zeigler, cellist and project creator

The work is centered around new compositions from Etienne Charles, Tamar-kali, Hannah Ishizaki and Jeffrey Zeigler; and features choreography/dance from Flexn pioneer Reggie “Regg Roc” Gray, and a bespoke interactive book design from sister sylvester.

The project is deeply rooted in an ethos of community and intergenerational learning – partnering with the Penn Center on St. Helena Island, South Carolina, the University of Georgia Culture & Community program and the Weeksville Heritage Center to devise community engagement and education platforms. After the sculptures are built and winners are declared in several categories, the sculptures remain on display to the general public for two weeks. At the close of the competition, all of the food is donated to Foodlink.

event.title: Happy Hallo-Green Makeup Workshop
event.description:
Get ready for Halloween with this one of-a-kind workshop! Learn the steps needed to go from “normal” to “unusual” from a professional makeup artist! Students will learn how to paint their faces green, give dimension to their work, and experiment with different techniques to transform into fun characters such as Frankenstein, witches, or even frogs! This workshop will make sure your Halloween look catches everyone’s eye!

Note: All participants will be using Mehron Makeup Paradise AQ, a water based green face paint, on themselves for the workshop. Participants should wear clothing they do not mind getting messy in.

This workshop is for guests ages 10 and up. A parent or guardian must accompany children under 16 and must also register for the program. Admission is limited and required pre-registration.

Kitty Lipski is a Theatrical Makeup artist based in Rochester, NY. She specializes in fantasy and high-concept characters, with a background in teaching the techniques. Kitty works at many local theatres as well as on touring Broadway shows, most notably the Wigs and Makeup Swing on the Broadway National Tour of “The Wiz”.

This Workshop occurs on both October 17 and 18.

event.title: College Night
event.description:
Gather your friends and enjoy an evening of play exclusively for college students! Play your way through the history of electronic games and pinball machines, put your skills to the test in the museum’s Ralph Wilson Skyline Climb ropes course, and explore the Dancing Wings Butterfly Garden (additional fees apply). Journey through childhood favorites like Sesame Street and Wegmans Super Kids Market and see new additions like Dollhouses Unveiled and Marble Speedway. Explore the World Video Game Hall of Fame, The National Toy Hall of Fame and try your hand at the world’s largest playable Donkey Kong arcade game, and much more!

Tickets are $15 in advance and $17 at the door. This program is only for current college students. Students must present a valid college ID at check-in. Tickets are nonrefundable.

event.title: LEGO Building Workshop

Participants will receive all the pieces they need and will be led step by step through the building process. At the end of the workshop, all participants can take their sets home to deconstruct and rebuild over and over again!

event.title: TACNY Junior Café Scientifique
event.description:
@

TACNY Junior Café Scientifique, a program for middle-school students, features discussions between STEM professionals/academics and students about topics in the fields of science, technology, engineering and mathematics in an informal atmosphere, and seeks to encourage students to consider careers in these areas. Students must be accompanied by an adult, and can explore the MOST at no cost immediately following the event. The program begins at 9:30, with continental breakfast available at 9:15. Attendees are welcome to spend the day at the MOST after the event.

See session details and RSVP information.

event.description:
@

Special for Veterans Day, watch the debut of “America the Beautiful,” playing every hour on the half hour, from 9:30 through 3:30 in the National Grid ExploraDome. FREE for all guests!

Reserve Free Tickets

America the Beautiful is a sweeping giant screen experience celebrating the vast and varied natural worlds that define the United States and the conservation movement that has ensured their survival. The protection of America’s beauty, wonder and resources was set in motion by Theodore Roosevelt and other pioneers who popularized principles still in practice today, passed down through generations, that will keep America’s wild heart beating for many more. Audiences will embark on an awe-inspiring journey from sea to shining sea, across the country’s most iconic and diverse environments – soaring mountain ranges, expansive plains, surprising deserts, flowing rivers and wetlands – captured with the scale, clarity, and immersion of spectacular giant screen cinematography.

event.title: Live Music | Meschiya Lake
event.cost: $22 for Members; $25 for non-members; $12 for students
event.description:
Join us for an evening of lush, intimate sound comprised of stringed instruments, vocal harmonies, and original compositions featuring local musician Meschiya Lake. 

ABOUT THE MUSICIAN 

Meschiya Lake is a dynamic addition to Asheville’s music scene, bringing her powerful vocals, captivating stage presence, and genre-spanning sound to audiences across Western North Carolina. After years of building an acclaimed career in New Orleans, Lake has made Asheville home, blending jazz, blues, Americana, and country influences into performances that are both timeless and fresh. Whether performing intimate originals or beloved classics, Meschiya’s heartfelt storytelling and infectious energy continue to win over local music lovers throughout the region. 

From the stages of Lincoln Center in New York City, to Brazil, Canada, Denmark, The Netherlands, Italy, Russia, the United Kingdom, and Ireland, Meschiya Lake has shown people to express love of life through music and dance.  This passion, seemingly tireless energy, and expert skill have garnered much praise, from NPR’s top ten albums of 2010 to First Lady of Jazz 2013, at the Sun Valley Jazz Festival. But most importantly, back at home in New Orleans, Lake was recognized as Female Performer of the Year, three years running, at the Big Easy Awards, and named Best Female Singer in Offbeat Magazine’s Best of the Beat poll in 2013 and 2014. 

For more information on Meschiya Lake please visit  www.meschiyalake.com

event.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum
event.cost: Free for Members (pre-registration required) and $15 for non-members
event.description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal.

The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibitions. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed.

Join Joshua on October 3, November 7, and December 5.

ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST

Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life.

Purchase Tickets

Please enter through the Staff Entrance to the left of the building.

event.title: Adult Studio: Beginner Drop Spinning
event.cost: $75 (Museum Members receive 10% discount with code at checkout; two partial scholarships for underserved populations; materials included)
event.description:
Your life is filled with textiles made from various spun threads and yarn. Come deepen those connections with the fibers that are deeply woven into many aspects of our lives by trying your hand at one of the earliest ways to handspin yarn using a drop spindle.

Join us for a fun, educational and meditative day of learning the top whirl dropspindle, and maybe some other styles as well. We will prepare, card and spin raw wool fleece to create yarn on a drop spindle. You may have time to try different types of fibers and even different types of spindles. You will get to take home your first handspun yarn, as well as a drop spindle to continue exploring this new skill.

ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST

Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the Southeastern United States, including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

event.cost: $10 for Members and $15 for non members
event.description:
Join us for an evening with New York-based artist Lesley Dill, whose work is featured in the current exhibition, The Art of Paper. Dill will talk about her projects that involve paper and collaboration, from huge community and large-scale installations to the intimate creation of artist books and sculptures, as well as her work with artists, poets, students, and studios, such as Tamarind and Dieu Donne. 

PAPER IS MY FRIEND: 

“Paper is about fingertip energy for me. The way one moves in to touch paper is like no other approach. It’s as if each finger has a little imaginary rocketship in it. We touch nothing else the way we touch paper. Paper is the medium of intimacy. The end result is wonder. All printmaking begins with the choice of what paper and in this way, it is about a relationship to fragility and force. This relationship comes from Poetry.” 

ABOUT THE ARTIST

Lesley Dill is an American artist working at the intersection of language and fine art in sculpture, printmaking, installation and performance, exploring the power of words to cloak and reveal the psyche. Dill has had over one hundred solo exhibitions. Her artworks are in the collections of many major museums, including the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Museum of Modern Art, New York. In 2017 she was named a fellow of The John Simon Guggenheim Foundation. Her opera, Divide Light, based on the poems of Emily Dickinson, was performed in San Jose in 2008, restaged in New York City in 2018, and captured in an award-winning film by Ed Robbins. Dill’s exhibition Wild Grace This Private Hallucinatory Moment at Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans (2025–26), a result of research conducted as a 2023–2024 Smithsonian Artist Research Fellow, examined themes of radiance and healing in seen and unseen energies. Dill’s exhibition Wilderness: Light Sizzles Around Me, organized by the Figge Art Museum and traveled to seven venues from 2021 to 2023, amplifies voices of the North American past as they wrestle with divinity, deviltry, and freedom, including Mother Ann Lee, Black Hawk, Sojourner Truth, John Brown, Emily Dickinson, Horace Pippin, and Sister Gertrude Morgan. Ms. Dill is represented by Arthur Roger Gallery in New Orleans. She lives and works in Brooklyn, New York. For more information and images of her work, visit www.lesleydill.net

Over 420,000 people flocked to the exhibition to marvel at Bosch’s curious creations, with opening hours extended to 1am to accommodate the phenomenal demand.

Accompanied by expert insights from the exhibition’s curators and leading cultural critics, the film delves into the life of the visionary artist to explore the inspiration behind his strange and haunting works. Contributors include maverick filmmaker and artist Peter Greenaway, The Times’ Chief Art Critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston, and Director of the Het Noordbrabants Museum Dr. Charles de Mooij.

The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch allows audiences to appreciate the detail of Bosch’s paintings like never before, offering close-up views of the curiosities hidden within his brimming canvases, from cannibalistic clergymen to three- headed birds.

After 20 years of chronicling his Puerto Rican family, a director and his mother craft animations that bring

William D. Caballero is an American filmmaker whose work merges documentary, animation, and
handcrafted miniature worlds to explore memory, migration, faith, and the emotional architecture of
family. Across film, television, and short-form media, Caballero has developed a singular visual language
rooted in tactile set-building, intergenerational storytelling, and a deep reverence for his Puerto Rican
heritage.
In 2001, he was awarded the prestigious Gates Millennium Scholarship, recognizing his academic promise
and leadership at an early stage in his career. He went on to earn a BFA from Pratt Institute in 2006 and an
MA from New York University in 2008. This foundation in both fine art and cinematic storytelling laid the
groundwork for a practice that bridges visual art, documentary realism, and experimental fabrication.
While at NYU, Caballero created American Dreams Deferred, his first (but not last) autobiographical
feature about his family.
Caballero first gained widespread recognition in 2015 as the creator of the HBO series Gran’Pa Knows
Best, which premiered on HBO and ran for two seasons. Centered on 3D-printed miniature recreations of
his Puerto Rican grandfather, the series combined playful scale with emotional depth, redefining what
personal storytelling could look like on television. Its inventive approach to memory and intergenerational
dialogue positioned Caballero as a bold new voice in hybrid nonfiction storytelling.

event.cost: $12 for Members; $15 for non-members (does not include Museum admission)
event.description:
For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. From Hansen’s beautiful house and gardens at Ordrupgaard to the streets of bohemian Paris, this film takes you on a journey to discover some of the best examples of 19th-century French art ever collected.

AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound.  The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story.  Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed more than 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music.

AmiciMusic is a chamber music organization based in Asheville and Baltimore dedicated to performing the highest quality chamber music in intimate venues and non-traditional spaces. This concert breaks down barriers between performers and audiences by setting up a more relaxed and informal atmosphere through informative talks about each composer’s life before each piece is played.

Add a VIP Ticket: Round out your concert experience by joining us from 5:45–6-45pm in the Museum’s Perspective Café for a pre-concert reception. Meet the musicians and your fellow concert goers while enjoying a drink and some light bites. Premium reserved seating for VIP ticket holders will allow you to join the concert just before start time.

About the Musicians

Since his solo debut with the legendary Philadelphia Orchestra at age nine, violinist Timothy Schwarz has had a brilliant career as a soloist, chamber musician, and pedagogue. Praised for his “energetic performances” (Rome News) and “technique beyond reproach” (Buffalo Times), Schwarz regularly performs throughout Europe, Asia, and the Americas as a soloist and chamber musician. His many recordings include the 2018 release of Anthems from Prometheus (Albany Records) “All credit to Timothy Schwarz for providing a performance as gripping from first to last as this one” (Fanfare Magazine), the 2013 release of Early Chamber Works by Jennifer Higdon (Naxos) “Top 10 Classical Albums in 2013” (Philadelphia City Paper) and his 2006 release of Timothy Schwarz, Live! “Good enough to be the only recording in your collection” (American Record Guide).  An avid educator, Schwarz is currently Assistant Professor and Head of Strings at Rowan University and Artistic Director and Founder of Techne Music, which includes a summer chamber music camp and concert series. For a five-year period through 2001, Schwarz served three tours as Artistic Ambassador in South America, Asia, and Africa, performing over 100 recitals in 15 countries. He received a Masters of Music from the Peabody Conservatory and a Doctorate of Musical Arts in Performance from Temple University. For further information and a performance schedule, visit www.TimothySchwarz.com.

event.title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
event.cost: $12 for Members; $15 for non-members (does not include Museum admission)
event.description:
For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. From Hansen’s beautiful house and gardens at Ordrupgaard to the streets of bohemian Paris, this film takes you on a journey to discover some of the best examples of 19th-century French art ever collected.

event.description:
Two hundred years after its opening and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh artworks, the National Gallery, London is hosting the United Kingdom’s biggest ever Van Gogh exhibition. Van Gogh is not only one of the most beloved artists of all time, but perhaps the most misunderstood.

This film is a chance to reexamine and better understand this iconic artist. Focusing on his unique creative process, Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers explores the artist’s years in the south of France, where he revolutionized his style. Van Gogh became consumed with a passion for storytelling in his art, turning the world around him into vibrant, idealized spaces and symbolic characters.

Poets and lovers filled his imagination; everything he did in the south of France served this new obsession. In part, this is what caused his notorious breakdown, but it didn’t hold back his creativity as he created masterpiece after masterpiece. Explore one of art history’s most pivotal periods in this once-in-a-century show. Made in close collaboration with the National Gallery.

event.cost: Free for Members or included with Museum admission
event.description:
Join us for a screening of Backside followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, Raúl O. Paz-Pastrana.

Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit.

Screening time: TBD

Film Synopsis:

Backside offers an intimate portrait of the migrant workers who endure long hours and often dangerous
working conditions year-round to prepare polished horses for “two minutes of glory.”
With the support of an all Latinx team of talented filmmakers and groom experts, Backside took five
years to make. The film peels back the layers of Churchill Downs’ barns (In Louisville, KY), known as the
“backside,” patiently revealing the symbiotic relationship between human and animal labor. Across a full
racing season, the expertise and grit of the workers are juxtaposed against the wealth and pageantry of
the Derby, exposing entrenched disparities of race and class that remain very much a part of the fabric of
the United States. In its essence, Backside is an ode—to the working class, and most profoundly, to the
immigrant workers who quietly sustain this country.
In today’s political climate, immigrants are often dehumanized and blamed for the poverty, violence and
declining living conditions in our country, ills we did not create. Backside invites viewers to look beyond
these incendiary words, to meet the people whose stories are rarely told. It asks audiences to witness
their lives, their dignity, their resilience—and, in doing so, to reflect on the vital role immi-grants play in
our communities.

About the filmmaker:

Raúl is a Mexican immigrant filmmaker, cinematographer and multimedia creator traversing borderlands
and migrant trails. His work intersects narrative fiction, participatory filmmaking, and visual ethnography
to explore themes of belonging, alienation and the concept of “home.”
Raúl’s films include “Backside” (2025 Tribeca / FICM, 85min.) a feature film about the migrant workforce
behind the Kentucky Derby, exploring the relationship between the thoroughbred horses and those who
care for them; “Border South” (2019 Sheffield / FICG, 84min.), which follows the clandestine migrant
routes from southern Mexico to the U.S.-Mexico border; and “The Stars are the Same” (2025 Aspen
ShortFest 12min.), which focuses on the experiences of an Indigenous Mayan elder who fled war-torn
Guatemala for southern Colorado. His films have screened worldwide including at the Tribeca Film
Festival, Sheffield Doc/Fest, the Aspen ShortFest, the Margaret Mead Film Festival, MASS MoCA
Museum, the Guadalajara International Film Festival, and the Morelia International Film Festival (FICM),
among many more. His work has received support from the Princess Grace Foundation, The Ford
Foundation, the LEF Foundation, ITVS, Catapult Film Fund, the Jerome Foundation, and the Sundance Institute, among others. Raúl is a Firelight Media Documentary Lab Fellow, a New America National Fellow, a Creative Capital Awards Artist Fellow, and a Guggenheim Fellow.

Screening time: 44:00:00

Film Synopsis:

Two Chinese-American storytellers uncover the untold history of Chinese immigrants in Memphis,
Tennessee, across a 150-year tapestry of identity and resilience.

About the filmmaker:

Thandi Cai (they/them) Director and Creator of Bluff City Chinese identifies as a storyteller of the Asian
Diaspora. Cai grew up in Memphis, TN where they learned how storytelling could be used to empower
themselves and others across racial, political, gender, ethnic and economic lines. Cai uses visual arts,
film-making, and graphic design to begin conversations around critical dialogue. Their goal as an artist is
to arouse imagination, pleasure, and improvisation to ideate new paths forward.
After earning a BS in Architectural Design, they served for two years as an education volunteer for Peace
Corps Lesotho until 2018. From there they were a teaching-artist, exploring the intersection of nonprofit
work, art, and community organizing. In 2022, they earned an MFA in Visual Communication Design at the
School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

event.title: Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert
event.description:
Ignite your inner calm with an evening of sound and shadow! October 8th, step out of the daily rush and into the glow. Mindful MAGiC: Candlelit Consciousness Concert invites you to experience our auditorium as never before—filled with gongs and transformed into a flickering sanctuary of over 200 candles.

Harold Taddy brings the sound bath element of MAG’s celebrated wellness series to the main stage, weaving a tapestry of tranquil soundscapes. To help guide your journey, this performance features poetic guided meditations by spoken word artist Theo Trombulak woven seamlessly throughout the experience, creating a space that is as intellectually stirring as it is restorative.

Part recital and part immersive meditation, this is a rare opportunity to experience “concert-style” mindfulness in a supportive, beautifully lit environment.

This is a seated experience—just bring yourself. Less movement, more MAGiC—just you and the sound.

Important Program Details

  • All guests must be seated by 6:30 pm to preserve the tranquil nature of the session. To ensure a peaceful atmosphere for all participants, late entry will not be permitted once the session is underway.
  • Food and beverages are not permitted in the galleries. Please use the designated cubby spaces in the Vanden Brul Pavilion for storage.
  • This is a seated experience in MAG’s auditorium. Seating is arranged in a theater-style configuration, offering clear views of the stage and excellent sound quality throughout the venue. Guests may choose their seats upon arrival on a first-come, first-served basis. For added comfort, feel free to bring a blanket and settle in for the experience.

For questions about this program, contact Katie Nguyen, Senior Manager of Guest Services, at knguyen@mag.rochester.edu.

Ticket sales end on Thursday, October 8, at 6:15 pm. Ticket includes museum admission. Member discount applies to the first two tickets in your order.

event.title: Going for Baroque
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Going for Baroque is a weekly series of mini-recitals at the Memorial Art Gallery. It is offered each Sunday at 1:30 pm and again at 3:00 pm. It offers the opportunity for students from the Eastman School of Music to perform alongside professional musicians on the Italian Baroque organ on the second floor of the museum. The 25-minute mini-recital is included with museum admission.

Owned by the Eastman School of Music, the fully restored Italian Baroque organ is the only full-size antique Italian organ in North America. The organ is the centerpiece of an installation that highlights more than 30 major Baroque-period paintings and sculptures.

event.title: Going for Baroque
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Going for Baroque is a weekly series of mini-recitals at the Memorial Art Gallery. It is offered each Sunday at 1:30 pm and again at 3:00 pm. It offers the opportunity for students from the Eastman School of Music to perform alongside professional musicians on the Italian Baroque organ on the second floor of the museum. The 25-minute mini-recital is included with museum admission.

Owned by the Eastman School of Music, the fully restored Italian Baroque organ is the only full-size antique Italian organ in North America. The organ is the centerpiece of an installation that highlights more than 30 major Baroque-period paintings and sculptures.

event.title: Museum of the Dead
event.description:
Do you like scary movies? Museum of the Dead is back with all your favorite (slightly) scary experiences—art, music, a costume contest, cocktails, fortune-telling, and food—it’s the party you cannot miss! Sign up early for your chance to save on tickets to get in on more activities, more friends, more fun, more giveaways, and more scares this year.

Ticket sales are open for everyone! There’s a $10 discount on general tickets through October 1 (applied at checkout).

Buy general tickets

VIP Experience—SOLD OUT!

Want the ultimate Museum of the Dead experience? MAG’s VIP hour is back! Your ticket includes exclusive Scream-tastic swag, entry to the VIP lounge (with dedicated bar), a discounted ticket to the food trucks, a complimentary drink, and a VIP photo op. You’ll also be able to register for tarot card readings and ghost tours during the VIP hour, as well as a few spots during the rest of the night.

Tarot Card Reading & Ghost Tours

Timed-ticket alert! Be sure to sign up ahead of time to secure a time slot with our fortune-tellers or a ghost tour with Monroe County Paranormal Investigations. (There’s no additional cost to reserving a spot for a reading or a tour, but space for both is limited.)

The links to register are shared in the confirmation email sent when you buy tickets. Please note that the registrations links for VIP guests are different from the links for general admission; please use the links provided.

Schedule of Events

7:00–8:00 pm | VIP hour

7:00–11:00 pm | Food Trucks

8:00–10:00 pm | Museum Galleries open for exploration

  • 8:15–9:45 pm | Tarot card reading (by registration) in Renaissance Gallery
  • 8:30–10:00 pm | Organ concert in the Fountain Court

8:00–11:00 pm | Party in Cutler Union & Vanden Brul Pavilion

  • 8:00–10:00 pm | Arts & Crafts in the M&T Bank Ballroom
  • 8:00–11:00 pm | Movie: Scream, shown in the M&T Bank Ballroom
  • 8:00–11:00 pm | Live DJ & Dancing, Step & Repeat Photo Op in the Vanden Brul Pavilion
  • 10:00 pm | Costume Contest winners announced in the Vanden Brul Pavilion

Costume Contest

Throughout the night, MAG staff members will be giving out cards to guests who qualify for the costume contest. Save your card, and meet at the Admissions Desk/entrance to the galleries at 9:50 pm, with the costume contest at 10 pm. If YOU think you qualify for the contest, find a MAG staff member and let them know, they might just give you a card!

At 10:00 pm, everyone will gather in the Vanden Brul Pavilion, and the DJ will announce the winners. Winners will get great prizes from local businesses!

Categories:

  • Best group
  • Best couple
  • Funniest
  • Most mind-blowing
  • Spookiest
  • Most inspired by MAG art

Parking and Maps

Museum of the Dead takes place at the Memorial Art Gallery (see on google maps). We have free on-site parking in our parking lots and on the grass. It’s available on a first-come, first-serve basis; we recommend checking out other available free parking in the Neighborhood of the Arts (NOTA) ahead of time, in case our lots are full when you arrive.

Once parked, you will enter MAG through the Cutler Union entrance (please follow the signs. You will see stairs and will go up to check-in). If you need wheelchair access, please go through MAG’s Main Entrance, where Security will lead you to check-in.

Maps of the grounds and interior will be available soon!

Guidelines

We have some special guidelines to make sure this event is fun for everyone!

  • Please arrive with your proof of identification. This event is 21+ only, and we will be checking everyone’s ID at check-in.
  • Tickets will not be sold at the door. Make sure you and your friends get them early! Sales end on Friday, October 23, at 6:00 pm.
  • Please print your tickets or have them ready to be scanned on a mobile device upon arrival. This helps make check-in quick and easy!
  • Please be mindful of the props and substances used in your costume. To protect the works in our galleries, we will have a place set up to check the following items before exploring the collection: swords, sabers, wings, spider legs, potions, broomsticks, feathers, sticky/slimy/wet/glittery substances. Please note: there may be additions to this list at the discretion of MAG staff.
  • Please leave weapons (costume or real—guns, knives, etc.), backpacks, and water bottles at home.
  • Please remember that MAG is a non-smoking campus. This includes smoking, vaping, and any recreational substances.
  • Please arrive by 9:30 pm. We want everyone to make the most of their time with us!
  • Please remember that there is no re-entry.

event.title: Art Lover’s Tour: Santa Fe
event.description:
Join us in Georgia O’Keeffe country and delve into the rich heritage of northern New Mexico on a journey that weaves together centuries-old craft traditions with the splendor of iconic sights.

Enjoy opportunities to engage directly with skilled local artisans, art curators, and gallery owners, whose insights reveal how ancestral knowledge, materials, and cultural values continue to shape living artistic traditions in the Southwest today. Visits to museums, Abiquiú, and Ghost Ranch situate artistic practice within the dramatic terrain that inspired generations of makers, painters, and writers. A visit to O’Keeffe’s studio reveals the deep connection between the artist and the creative vision she cultivated there for more than four decades. In Chimayo, examine the continuity of devotional art, weaving, and vernacular architecture rooted in centuries-old Hispano traditions. Throughout, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine defined by the use of heirloom ingredients and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel both ancient and inventive.

To be added to the waitlist for this tour, contact Emily Whitson, Distant Horizons, at 562-983-8828 or emilyw@distant-horizons.com.

 

Tour Highlights

  • Enjoy a tour of the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum pairing iconic paintings with personal objects that illuminate her deep connection to the New Mexico landscape.
  • Meet with gallery owner Andrea Fisher, a premier authority on New Mexico Pueblo pottery who maintains close relationships with artists.
  • Go behind-the-scenes at the Museum of International Folk Art with Laura Addison, one of the world’s largest museums dedicated to folk art.
  • Basketry was one of the first craft forms practiced by Indigenous communities and learn about the various styles at the Adobe Gallery.
  • Be part of a curated visit to O’Keefe’s home at Abiquiú, and understand how the landscape inspired her with a visit to nearby Ghost Ranch.
  • Visit Evoke Gallery and meet with director Katherine Erickson. Evoke emphasizes contemporary figurative painting and representational art.
  • Visit the IAIA’s Museum of Contemporary Native Arts and be joined by Manuela Well Off Man, chief curator for a very special visit.
  • Explore the Santuario de Chimayo, the second most important Catholic pilgrimage center in the United States.
  • Accompanied by Patricia Trujillo-Oviedo learn about the weaving traditions of Chimayo. She is a seventh generation descendant of original local settlers.
  • Throughout the program, enjoy Santa Fe’s cuisine and deeply rooted regional flavors that feel are both ancient and inventive. New Mexico blends Native American, Hispanic, and Anglo traditions in dishes that celebrate locally grown ingredients.

Our ART LOVER’S tours are organized and sponsored by the MAG Council to benefit MAG and are open to all interested travelers.

For more information or a more detailed brochure, email Michelle Turner at mt1@rochester.rr.com or Emily Whitson at emilyw@Distant-Horizons.com. For questions or assistance, please contact the MAG Council at magcouncil@mag.rochester.edu or 585.276.8910.

Anyone unable to attend a MAG Council Art Tour must make their request for a refund by contacting the MAG Council Office prior to the event registration deadline. For international/overnight tour refunds, the policy of the managing travel agency will take precedence.

If it is necessary for the MAG Council to cancel an Art Lover’s Tour, all payments made will be refunded in full.

The Memorial Art Gallery’s tour operator, Distant Horizons, is a California Seller of Travel (CST #2046776-40) and a participant in the California Travel Restitution Fund. Information regarding the rights of California residents to make a claim may be found at tcrcinfo.org. California law requires certain sellers of travel to have a trust account or bond. Distant Horizons has a trust account.

event.title: Art, Death, and Fashion DeTOUR
event.description:
Advanced medicines, skincare creams, surgeries, and social media filters help us to stave off the idea of aging and death — but what have we lost in the process? Join fashion historian Brandon W. Brooks for a spooky season MAGsocial DeTOUR℠, as he examines the intersection of art and our former deathways. How is the ever-present reality of death reflected in art, fashion, and memory? How might art and fashion temper our anxieties surrounding death, or shape our grief for a lost loved one? Have we all forgotten how to mourn fashionably, or is it all just a bunch of hocus pocus?

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the tour.

For questions about this event, please contact MAG Engagement Manager Jessica Gasbarre at jgasbarre@mag.rochester.edu. Ticket sales end on Thursday, October 29, at 6:15 pm. Ticket includes DeTOUR℠ and museum admission.

Brought to you by MAGsocial.

event.description:
Awaken your senses and settle into stillness with a morning practice that weaves together gentle movement and enveloping sound. Held in the tranquil Fountain Court, this unique session offers Kundalini yoga guided by Karen Cringoli of Frequency Wellness, set to the transformative tones of live gong and sound by Harold Taddy (The Gong Situation).

  • Yoga mat, bolsters, and layers for comfort
  • Cozy socks
  • A water bottle with a secure, leak-proof lid (no straws)

  • Doors open at 9:00 am
  • Check-in at the Admissions Desk no later than 9:15 am to get situated
  • Please arrive on time to preserve the tranquil nature of the session

The session lasts 9:30–10:30 am, followed by a 15-minute courtesy window to ease your transition into the day. Museum admission begins at 11:00 am when the galleries open to the public.

Come curious. Move with intention. Let the sound guide you.

event.title: Chasing Rainbows: How We Talk About Color
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Color is one of the most foundational experiences we have as humans—yet our understanding about what color is, how we experience it, and how to talk about it is a bit squishy. Is aqua blue or green (or neither)? Does that change when you put aqua next to a blue or green? And if it does change, does that mean it’s still aqua? Science can provide answers—but what happens when the answers science gives us contradict our own experiences? Even artists who work with color all the time sometimes struggle with how to order, describe, and work with color. Is there a common language we can all use?

Join lexicographer and author Kory Stamper as she guides you through a kaleidoscopic journey through modern color science, color psychology, color naming and descriptions, and our perceptions about color using artworks in the MAG collection.

Kory Stamper is an author and lexicographer who has spent near 30 years thinking (too deeply) about how to define the words that define us. In her 20 years as an editor at Merriam-Webster, she defined everything from “blue plate special” to “god” and answered dictionary user questions on everything from what color “nude” really is to why it’s “toothpaste” and not “teethpaste.” She has written about her time as a dictionary writer in Word by Word: The Secret Life of Dictionaries (2017, Pantheon). Her moderate obsession with color began during her time at Merriam-Webster, and led to her second nonfiction book, True Color: The Strange and Spectacular Quest to Define Color—from Azure to Zinc Pink (2026, Knopf).

Lecture will be followed by a book signing in the Vanden Brul Pavilion until 8:30 pm.

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the program.

Advance registration is required for this free event. Capacity is limited. Registration closes on Tuesday, November 10, at 7:00 pm.

For questions or assistance, please contact memberperks@mag.rochester.edu.

event.cost: Free – $10
event.description:
During this month’s Second Friday, MAG invites you to draw the likeness of the people you come with! Be as creative, crazy, or serious as you want in your masterpiece. Then, switch places, so you become the muse! Pro tip: grab one of our folding black stools for a more comfortable seat as you draw in the galleries.

Attending Second Friday solo? We have you covered! Grab your pencil and paper to doodle one of the portraits in MAG’s collection—stop by the Admissions Desk for ideas!

Don’t forget to stop by the Brown Hound Downtown bar in the Vanden Brul Pavilion for this month’s featured pints. Plus, everyone receives half-price admission from 5:00-8:00 pm!

event.title: Faculty Open House
event.cost: Free
event.description:
Faculty, friends, and fellow educators—join us for an evening at the Memorial Art Gallery specifically for you! Faculty and staff from colleges and universities throughout the Rochester region are invited to join us for an event designed to connect with colleagues, discover new resources, and explore how access to MAG can enrich your courses. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the museum, complete with light fare, a signature cocktail special, a presentation by MAG’s University Liaison Lauren Tagliaferro, gallery tours, and opportunities to mingle with MAG staff and fellow educators

Bring a colleague and spend an evening connecting, exploring, and getting inspired! Plus, learn how MAG can support learning, research, and engagement across disciplines.

To submit a request for ASL interpretation, please email access@mag.rochester.edu at least two weeks before the event.

For questions about this event, please contact MAG’s University Liaison Lauren Tagliaferro at ltagliaferro@mag.rochester.edu. Registration ends on Friday, November 13, at 5:30 pm. Ticket includes museum admission.

Taught by: Jason Ferguson

Spin, shape, and laugh your way through this two-hour beginner pottery workshop. Learn the basics of throwing clay on the wheel, no experience needed! Come solo or with your favorite people and keep one bowl to decorate and make totally yours. Work will be ready in two to three weeks following the class.

Materials

All materials provided.

For safety, please wear closed-toe shoes, have your long hair pulled back/up, and keep your nails trimmed. We will contact you via email when your work is ready in two to three weeks.

Registration Information

Registration for this program starts on Tuesday, August 18, at 10:00 am for MAG Members, and Tuesday, August 25, at 10:00 am for Not-Yet-Members. Online registration ends on Friday, November 13, at 12:00 pm.
